ruling.recommended_action: Refund the metered overcharge on the 13:07–13:13 off-route segment (2.21 km × $1.4099/km = $3.12 SGD) to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7; the 12:49–12:55 segment and the metered waiting unit stay billed.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so extra kilometres run on the meter and route-deviation refunds are measured per kilometre rather than by a fixed quote [F8][RD-2]. The record contains exactly two off-route segments — 12:49–12:55 (+1.31 km) and 13:07–13:13 (+2.21 km) — and each must be examined separately for exemption under RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 [F3][F4][RD-1].

Segment F3 (12:49–12:55, +1.31 km): the driver asked at 12:46 "Jam on Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3 is building up ahead, can I go round via Serangoon Garden Way?" [F9], and the rider answered at 12:47 "Sure, go ahead." [F10]. That rider message is timestamped before the segment started at 12:49 and the chat record is complete, both messages timestamped [F11], so this is a named-road authorisation read in context. The rider's words "go ahead" adopt the driver's named route, and the segment is the deviation made to take that route; the exemption applies to the earlier segment the authorisation was given for [F9][F10][RD-5]. Neither side now disputes this — the rider withdrew the claim on F3 and the driver claims exemption only for it [F3][RD-5]. It is therefore exempt.

Segment F4 (13:07–13:13, +2.21 km): nothing ties this later segment to Serangoon Garden Way. There is no rider message between 12:47 and the 13:07 start — the chat holds only two messages, all timestamped [F11] — and the driver's own post-trip statement says "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" [F12]. A driver's statement is not rider consent (G11), and the trace places no road name on the driven path, so the specific authorisation to Serangoon Garden Way does not cover a deviation twenty minutes later that the driver himself attributes to rerouting [F12][RD-5]. The general-consent branch does not help either: the rider's words were a specific named-road authorisation, not "whichever way is faster", and a reroute of the driver's own initiative is not an errand the rider authorised [F9][F10][RD-5]. Resolution: this segment is unexempted.

No traffic excuse is available for F4. The only incident screen shows no incident near the route during the trip window [F15], and the only speed-band records are CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY and ANG MO KIO AVENUE 3 at band 5 (40–49 km/h), which are not band 1–2 congestion and in any case cannot exempt a segment on their own [F13][F14][RD-4]. Weather is fair, so no cause there either [F16]. The 2.21 extra kilometres on F4 are therefore refundable under RD-2 [F4][RD-2].

The amount follows the trace formula: this trip's per-kilometre rate is the fare record's distance fare divided by distance km, $33.02 ÷ 23.42 km = $1.4099/km [F5][F8]. Refundable extra km = the unexempted segment only, 2.21 km [F4]: 2.21 km × $1.4099/km = $3.1159 → $3.12 [F4][F5][F8][RD-2]. The exempt 1.31 km of F3 and the residual gap between the 4.29 km billed in F5 and the 3.52 km of F3+F4 (the 0.77 km of route-corridor/matching slack) are not refunded [F3][F5][RD-2]. The metered waiting unit of $0.11 for 0.4 min is a RydeTAXI waiting unit and is not part of the dispute [F6][F8][RD-3].

Account flag is not engaged: RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 and the driver's profile shows 1 dispute total, 1 upheld, route: 0, so this case does not make the conduct "repeated"; profile facts cannot decide liability in any event [F17][F18][RD-6]. The drivers' and riders' profiles therefore change nothing in the outcome [F17][F18].

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint. They concern a jam, a route around it, a second unannounced turn-off and a refund request. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere in them [F9][F10][F12] — finding is "none" [RD-1 conditions aside, SAFE-1 screen applied].
